lines.text: What if time itself had a master?
In Hindu tradition, Kala Bhairava is worshipped as the Lord of Time…
the divine force beyond birth, death, and destruction.
But why is Bhairava given this extraordinary title?
The word Kala carries a powerful meaning.
It represents time…
and it also represents death.
Everything in this universe is controlled by time.
Kings rise…
empires fall…
stars are born…
and entire worlds eventually disappear.
Nothing can escape its passage.
But Kala Bhairava represents the divine power that stands beyond these limitations.
He reminds us that time waits for no one…
and that every action has its consequences.
In his fierce form, Bhairava destroys arrogance, ignorance, and the illusion that life will last forever.
He is also worshipped as the guardian of Kashi…
the sacred city where devotees seek liberation from the cycle of birth and death.
His presence teaches a profound lesson.
Do not waste the time you have been given.
Use it to follow dharma…
overcome your ego…
and move closer to the truth.
For everything in this universe is temporary.
But the eternal reality beyond time…
can never be destroyed.
That is why devotees remember him as Kala Bhairava…
the Lord who governs time and reminds all beings of their ultimate destiny.
But how did this terrifying form of Lord Shiva become the protector of devotees?
And why is a dog always seen beside him?
That is the mystery we will uncover in the next episode.
